extracted.intended_audience: aspiring authors seeking literary agents / writers seeking representation
extracted.subtask_description: Information and resources for authors trying to locate and approach literary agents (agency directory profile, agent vetting, and preparation of submission materials). Emphasizes directory data, submission methods, genre alignment, and optional coaching services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Directory listing contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent bios for all agents at the Creative Artists Agency; AAR membership status; Personal email addresses; Mailing addresses; Agent photos; Preferred query letter methods (email, online form, postal mail); A link to the Creative Artists Agency website; A map to the office of the Creative Artists Agency; Access to all literary agent profiles in the Directory of Literary Agents; Search the directory by book genre/category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page presents this as the set of data fields the directory provides — these are the items an author should expect/seek when using an agent directory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Directory accuracy / currency
rubrics_metrics.description: Most literary agency directories (print and online) are outdated, incomplete, and riddled with mistakes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warning: relying on outdated/inaccurate directories will hurt your chances of getting an agent. Prefer up-to-date, comprehensive directories and verify agent contact/submission details before querying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare required submission materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Support areas listed: Book Development; Query Letter; Book Synopsis; Book Proposal; Author Platform; Agent Selection; Process/Strategy; Troubleshooting; Miscellaneous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should prepare these core materials (especially a targeted query letter, polished synopsis, and proposal where applicable) and develop an author platform and strategy before approaching agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow agents' preferred query methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred query letter methods (email, online form, postal mail).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine and use each agent's stated preferred submission method rather than sending queries arbitrarily; the directory claims to list preferred methods so use that information to comply with agent preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vet agents and their credentials
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent bios and AAR membership status are provided in listings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use agent bios and AAR (Association of Authors' Representatives) membership status as vetting signals when selecting whom to query; verify contact details and agency information (website link, office map) before outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target agents by genre
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews/Tips from Successful Authors are organized by genre (Children's Books, Fiction/Novels subgenres, Memoir/Autobiography, Narrative Nonfiction subgenres, Nonfiction Books categories).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek agents who represent your specific genre/category and consult genre-specific interviews and tips to learn agent expectations and submission norms for that category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider professional coaching/consulting
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bestselling Author offers 1-on-1 coaching and consulting (services include Literary Agent Advice, scheduling a 1-on-1 Author Consultation, and claims of having helped 400+ writers get offers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may improve chances by using paid coaching for query letters, proposals, agent selection, and strategy; evaluate coaching providers' track record and testimonials before purchasing services.
